title: Prime Time: Factors, Multiples and Primes
seo_title: Prime Time Class 6 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 5)
standard_text: Common multiples and common factors, prime and composite numbers, co-prime numbers, prime factorisation and divisibility tests (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 6)
meta_desc: Class 6 Prime Time worksheet (Ganita Prakash Chapter 5): factors, multiples, common factors, primes, co-primes, prime factorisation and divisibility tests. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself
body_html:
How it works

A factor divides a number exactly; a multiple is in its times table. A prime has exactly two factors (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, …); a composite number has more.

Two numbers are co-prime if their only common factor is 1, like 8 and 15. Every number can be written as a product of primes: 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.

Divisibility: by 2, 5, 10 look at the last digit; by 4 the last two digits; by 8 the last three; by 3 and 9 the digit sum.

Example

Find the prime factorisation of 84.

84 = 2 × 42 = 2 × 2 × 21

Answer: 2 × 2 × 3 × 7

Example

Are 14 and 25 co-prime?

Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14

Factors of 25: 1, 5, 25

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

  • Calling 1 a prime number.
  • Thinking every odd number is prime (9, 15 and 21 are not).
  • Mixing up factors and multiples.

faq.a: No. A prime has exactly two factors; 1 has only one factor.
Two numbers whose only common factor is 1, such as 9 and 16.

faq.q: How do you test divisibility by 4?
faq.a: Check whether the number made by the last two digits is divisible by 4.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 24?
items.e: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 with no remainder, so 3 is a factor of 24. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which of these is a prime number?
items.e: 47 has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 69 = 3 × 23; 51 = 3 × 17; 81 = 3 × 27

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 6?
items.e: 54 = 6 × 9, so 54 is in the 6 times table. A multiple is the number times a whole number.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 64?
items.e: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 with no remainder, so 4 is a factor of 64. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 42?
items.e: 42 ÷ 21 = 2 with no remainder, so 21 is a factor of 42. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 60?
items.e: 60 ÷ 12 = 5 with no remainder, so 12 is a factor of 60. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 15?
items.e: 150 = 15 × 10, so 150 is in the 15 times table. A multiple is the number times a whole number.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 8?
items.e: 40 = 8 × 5, so 40 is in the 8 times table. A multiple is the number times a whole number.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 96?
items.e: 96 ÷ 8 = 12 with no remainder, so 8 is a factor of 96. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 54?
items.e: 54 ÷ 27 = 2 with no remainder, so 27 is a factor of 54. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 11?
items.e: 55 = 11 × 5, so 55 is in the 11 times table. A multiple is the number times a whole number.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 84?
items.e: 84 ÷ 12 = 7 with no remainder, so 12 is a factor of 84. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which of these is not a prime number?
items.e: 27 is not prime: 27 = 3 × 9, so it has more than two factors.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 75?
items.e: 75 ÷ 25 = 3 with no remainder, so 25 is a factor of 75. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 36?
items.e: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 with no remainder, so 9 is a factor of 36. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 7?
items.e: 49 = 7 × 7, so 49 is in the 7 times table. A multiple is the number times a whole number.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 48?
items.e: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 with no remainder, so 8 is a factor of 48. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 12?
items.e: 72 = 12 × 6, so 72 is in the 12 times table. A multiple is the number times a whole number.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 63?
items.e: 63 ÷ 21 = 3 with no remainder, so 21 is a factor of 63. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 45?
items.e: 45 ÷ 15 = 3 with no remainder, so 15 is a factor of 45. A factor divides into the number exactly.

items.q: How many common multiples of 6 and 9 are there from 1 to 50?
items.e: Common multiples are multiples of 18: 18, 36. That is 2.

items.q: Which pair of numbers is co-prime (their only common factor is 1)?
items.e: 25 and 27 have no common factor except 1, so they are co-prime.

items.q: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 30 and 12.
items.e: Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The biggest number in both lists is 6.

items.q: Write 112 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 4 times, 7 appears 1 time. So 112 = 24 × 7.

items.q: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 54 and 90.
items.e: Factors of 54: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, 27, 54. Factors of 90: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 15, 18, 30, 45, 90. The biggest number in both lists is 18.

items.q: Write 12 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 2 times, 3 appears 1 time. So 12 = 22 × 3.

items.q: Write 108 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 2 times, 3 appears 3 times. So 108 = 22 × 33.

items.q: Write 40 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 3 times, 5 appears 1 time. So 40 = 23 × 5.

items.q: Write 300 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 2 times, 3 appears 1 time, 5 appears 2 times. So 300 = 22 × 3 × 52.

items.q: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6.
items.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, … The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 12. (4 × 6 = 24 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.)

items.q: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 36 and 60.
items.e: Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. The biggest number in both lists is 12.

items.q: Write 98 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 1 time, 7 appears 2 times. So 98 = 2 × 72.

items.q: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 30 and 75.
items.e: Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Factors of 75: 1, 3, 5, 15, 25, 75. The biggest number in both lists is 15.

items.q: Write 140 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 2 times, 5 appears 1 time, 7 appears 1 time. So 140 = 22 × 5 × 7.

items.q: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 9 and 15.

items.q: 24 boys and 36 girls are put into teams. Every team must have the same number of boys and the same number of girls. What is the greatest number of teams?
items.e: The greatest common factor of 24 and 36 is 12.

items.q: 16 boys and 40 girls are put into teams. Every team must have the same number of boys and the same number of girls. What is the greatest number of teams?
items.e: The greatest common factor of 16 and 40 is 8.

items.q: 28 boys and 42 girls are put into teams. Every team must have the same number of boys and the same number of girls. What is the greatest number of teams?
items.e: The greatest common factor of 28 and 42 is 14.

items.q: In the idli-vada game, children count 1, 2, 3, … and say ‘idli’ for multiples of 3 and ‘vada’ for multiples of 4. Which is the first number where they say ‘idli-vada’?
items.e: The first common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12.

items.q: In the idli-vada game, children count 1, 2, 3, … and say ‘idli’ for multiples of 4 and ‘vada’ for multiples of 6. Which is the first number where they say ‘idli-vada’?
